introduction: In West Bengal, registering a marriage ensures its legal validity under the law. The registration is facilitated via the centralized MARREG (Marriage Registration) Portal under the Law Department.
quickFacts:
Important to Know
  • State: West Bengal
  • Portal: MARREG (Registrar General of Marriages, West Bengal)
  • Relevant Acts: The Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 & The Special Marriage Act, 1954 (selectable based on religion/type of marriage).
  • Mandatory Attendees: The Groom, the Bride, and exactly 3 Witnesses must physically appear for the final verification.
  • Biometrics: Fingerprint verification via Aadhaar is mandatory for the couple and all 3 witnesses during the physical visit.
documentsRequired:
Documents Required

Note: You must have the original and scanned (PDF) versions of the following documents.
Personal & Identity Proofs
  • Photographs: Recent passport-size photographs of the Groom and Bride.
  • Proof of Date of Birth (DOB): Birth Certificate is preferred. If you do not have one, you can use an Aadhaar Card, Pan Card, or 10th Admit Card/Pass Certificate, but you must select a valid reason from the dropdown menu (e.g., "Do not have birth registration") explaining why you aren't uploading a birth certificate.
  • Original Aadhaar Cards: Required for the Bride, Groom, and the 3 Witnesses during the offline visit.
Address & Marriage Proof
  • Proof of Address (Present & Permanent): Aadhaar Card, Voter ID Card, Passport, Ration Card, etc.
  • Proof of Social Marriage: A supporting document such as the Marriage Invitation Card.
onlineApplication:
Method 1: Apply Online via MARREG Portal

This includes the online form submission and the subsequent mandatory offline visit as explained in the video:

Step-by-Step Process:
  1. Step 1: Visit the official website: Go to rgmwb.gov.in.
  2. Step 2: Start Application: Click on "Register Your Marriage" and then select "Click Here to Apply Online".
  3. Step 3 (User Registration): Fill in your Name, Gender, DOB, Email ID, and Mobile Number. Verify the email and mobile number to generate a Registration ID.
  4. Step 4 (Login): Log in using your Registration ID.
  5. Step 5 (Application Form): Select the relevant act (e.g., The Hindu Marriage Act, 1955) and complete the 6-step form:
    • Personal Details: Fill in the groom's and bride's details (Name, Guardians, DOB, Religion, Aadhaar number, Occupation, and Marital Status).
    • Address: Fill out the Present and Permanent addresses for both.
    • Photo and Documents: Upload the passport photos, DOB proof, and Address proofs.
    • Details of Social Marriage: Enter the venue/address of your social marriage and the date. (Pro-tip: If you are applying before the actual wedding, select a future date to allow processing time). Upload the marriage invitation card.
    • Details of Children: Fill this out only if you have children from a previous or current arrangement.
    • Marriage Officer Details: Choose whether you want an officer near the Groom's or Bride's address. The portal will show a list of local Marriage Officers along with their names, office addresses, and contact numbers. Select one.
    • Registration Details: Choose whether the registration will happen at the officer's office or an outside venue, and pick a proposed registration date and time.
  6. Step 6: Submit Form: Check all declaration boxes, enter the CAPTCHA, and click "Submit".
  7. Step 7: Print Documents: Print out the submitted Application Form and the Application Receipt.
  8. Step 8 (Mandatory Offline Visit): On the allotted date, the Bride, Groom, and 3 Witnesses must visit the selected Marriage Officer's office. You must carry the printed application form, all original documents, and a set of Xerox copies.
  9. Step 9: Biometrics & Fees: The officer will take biometrics (fingerprints) of the bride, groom, and the 3 witnesses using their Aadhaar cards. You will pay the required registration fees directly to the officer at this time.
offlineApplication:
Method 2: Apply Offline

While the West Bengal Government highly encourages using the MARREG portal, offline applications can generally be processed as follows:

Step-by-Step Process:
  1. Step 1: Visit the Local Office: Visit your local Sub-Divisional Magistrate (SDM) office or the office of a local registered Marriage Officer/Registrar in your jurisdiction.
  2. Step 2: Request Form: Request the physical Marriage Registration Application Form.
  3. Step 3: Fill Details: Fill out the form manually with the details of the bride, groom, and the 3 witnesses.
  4. Step 4: Attach Documents: Attach your passport-size photographs and self-attested photocopies of your age proof, address proof, and the marriage invitation card.
  5. Step 5: Submit Form: Submit the application with the required cash fee to the officer.
  6. Step 6: Physical Verification & Biometrics: You will be given an appointment date. You, your spouse, and your 3 witnesses must physically appear on this date with all original documents for signature and biometric verification to complete the process.
afterApplying:
After Applying — What Next?

Contact the Officer

It is highly recommended to call the selected Marriage Officer (using the phone number provided on the portal during step 5) to confirm your appointment time, clarify the exact fee amount, and confirm if they need any extra photocopies.

Wait for the Certificate

Once the physical verification, signatures, and biometrics are successfully completed at the marriage officer's desk, the marriage is legally registered. The officer will issue the physical Marriage Certificate to you.

Document Safety

Keep the original Marriage Certificate safe, as you will need it for joint bank accounts, passport updates, visa applications, and other legal documentation.
